patient.chief_complaint: New onset unresponsiveness with eye deviation, subtle lip-smacking, EEG shows periodic discharges — expert disagreement about whether to treat
patient.history_present_illness: A 52-year-old White male middle school teacher was referred urgently from a community hospital neurology service after developing new-onset unresponsiveness. He had been admitted for evaluation of three days of progressive behavioral changes and word-finding difficulty. His wife reports that for three weeks he had been increasingly forgetful, getting lost on familiar routes, and last week had an episode where he stared blankly for 2 minutes with subtle lip movements — not recognized as a seizure at the time. He has no prior epilepsy. He was admitted to the outside hospital, started on IV acyclovir empirically, and transferred when his EEG showed 'concerning' periodic discharges. He has a history of moderate alcohol use (6-8 drinks per day for 20 years) and stopped drinking abruptly 5 days ago when symptoms began. Vitals on transfer: BP 148/88, HR 96, temp 37.2°C, SpO2 97%. On examination he appears to stare distantly, with slow intermittent eye deviation to the right, and subtle lip-smacking movements. He responds minimally to his name. His wife reports his baseline was completely normal 3 weeks ago. She denies any fever at home, no travel, no sick contacts, no new medications. Family history: father with Alzheimer's dementia. No family history of epilepsy. Past medical history: alcohol use disorder, hepatic steatosis, hypertension.

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG. Right temporal-occipital (T4-O2 maximal) lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs) at 1.2-1.8 Hz with superimposed fast activity ('LPD plus' features) — quasi-continuous throughout the recording. This pattern falls on the ictal-interictal continuum (IIC) per modified Salzburg consensus criteria; electrographic seizure criteria are not definitively met. A benzodiazepine diagnostic trial may be clinically useful to assess response. No prior EEG available for comparison. Clinical correlation recommended.
eeg.limitations: Ambiguous ictal-interictal continuum pattern; clinical correlation essential.

results.title: Paraneoplastic neurological syndromes: diagnosis and treatment
results.key_finding: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) is associated with SCLC in >80% of cases. Paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis with anti-Hu has poor prognosis compared to anti-LGI1/NMDAR because Hu targets intracellular antigens causing direct neuronal destruction. Tumor treatment (SCLC chemotherapy) is the primary treatment — immunotherapy alone has limited efficacy. NCSE in paraneoplastic encephalitis responds to AEDs + immunotherapy but neurological improvement is modest.

output.summary: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) antibody-associated paraneoplastic neurological syndrome is most frequently associated with small cell lung carcinoma (approximately 75-80% of cases) and other neuroendocrine tumors. The Hu antigen is intracellular, which is associated with a lower rate of neurological improvement with immunotherapy compared to antibodies targeting cell-surface antigens. Tumor-directed therapy is the primary management approach in published case series. Limbic encephalitis is the most common neurological phenotype; seizures and EEG abnormalities including LPDs and NCSE have been reported. Prognosis is generally guarded; outcome is correlated with tumor response to therapy.

Thiamine must be administered BEFORE glucose in alcoholic with documented deficiency.

critical_actions: Administer IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg first-line — also diagnostic for IIC
Empiric IV acyclovir until HSV PCR returns
IV thiamine 500 mg TID BEFORE any glucose given documented deficiency
Load levetiracetam to therapeutic level post-diagnostic trial confirmation

contraindicated_actions: Do NOT attribute encephalopathy to alcohol withdrawal alone — outside window and subacute decline pre-cessation
Do NOT under-dose thiamine — 500 mg IV TID is treatment dose; 100 mg is prophylactic
Do NOT continue acyclovir after HSV PCR confirmed negative
Do NOT delay tumor identification — immunotherapy alone is inadequate for anti-Hu
key_reasoning_points: Ictal-interictal continuum resolves with benzodiazepine diagnostic trial — clinical and EEG improvement confirms NCSE
Anti-Hu strongly associates with SCLC; intracellular-antigen syndromes respond poorly to immunotherapy alone — tumor-directed therapy is essential
Alcohol withdrawal seizures occur 6-48 hours after cessation, not 5 days later
Subacute 3-week behavioral decline pre-dating alcohol cessation is the paraneoplastic timeline
Wernicke needs 500 mg IV TID thiamine, not 100 mg/day prophylactic dosing
